title: These Midterm Races Will Decide Data Centers’ Political Fate
gist: Wired's Power Play column maps how data centers have become a bipartisan midterm political liability, with candidates in Senate, House and governor races attacking rivals as pro-data center, 20+ governor candidates promising moratoriums, and 30+ local ballot measures, over half in Ohio. It also notes Atoco's waste-heat water harvesting and Oracle trucking in natural gas to power a data center.

insights.claim: Public opinion has rapidly turned against data centers since the start of the year, with bipartisan opposition and many Republicans breaking with President Trump, and candidates on both sides attacking opponents as pro-data center.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Political risk for data center buildout is rising and could affect permitting, tax incentives and power cost recovery.
insights.quote: The opposition is bipartisan, with many Republicans making a rare break from President Donald Trump.

insights.claim: Data centers are potent enough to swing tight races and the balance of power in Congress, although pocketbook issues are likely to be top of voters' minds.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Midterm results on November 3 may shape federal and state data center policy.

insights.claim: At least 20 of 36 gubernatorial candidates have promised some kind of data center moratorium if elected, per Multistate, while the only true hyperscale moratorium in place was signed in July by New York governor Kathy Hochul.
